newsitem.title: USA: Cominco sees Western refined zinc stocks falling.
newsitem.headline: Cominco sees Western refined zinc stocks falling.

text.p: Cominco Ltd said it expects Western world refined zinc stocks to fall 300,000 tonnes this year as 3 percent growth in Western zinc demand pushes up the average LME monthly zinc price to between 50 and 60 cents a lb, David Thompson, the Canadian company's president and CEO, told an industry gathering.

Zinc prices ended last year in the high 40 cents a lb after Western world inventory fell 200,000 tonnes despite growth of minus-0.3 percent because of destocking by consumers, Thompson said in a presentation at the American Zinc Assocation annual meeting here.
Despite being one of the world's biggest producers of refined zinc, Cominco bought more than 70,000 tonnes of metal from the LME warehouses in the last two years.
"Demand from our customers in 1997 has started strongly and, if it is maintained, Cominco alone might have to purchase 50,000 tonnes of LME zinc this year," Thompson said.

Western world zinc stocks will return to normal levels this year with prices rising gradually. "However, a significant increase may still be some months away and perhaps the best year of the decade so far could well be 198," Thompson said.

Cominco's mined production is set to rise from about 550,000 tonnes of contained zinc to over 700,000 tonnes by 1999, with refined metal output increasing from about 370,000 tonnes this year to over 400,000 tonnes in 1998.

Western world zinc consumption is set to reach about 6.4 million tonnes this year, Cominco said, but there was still a deficit of refined Western world zinc capacity. Imports from Russia and China, along with running down stocks, will plug a gap of about one million tonnes, Thompson added.
